title: Framework: dot, normSq, arcLen, tripleProduct, projPerp
content: The proof uses Fin 3 → ℝ (function type) as the ambient vector space, compatible with Mathlib's crossProduct bilinear map. Six definitions are introduced: dot (inner product as ∑ uᵢvᵢ), normSq (= dot u u), IsUnit3 (normSq u = 1), arcLen (= Real.arccos of dot product), tripleProduct (= dot a (b×c), the scalar triple product / determinant), and projPerp (= fun i => uᵢ − (u·w)wᵢ, the perpendicular projection). This 'Fin 3 → ℝ' framework avoids EuclideanSpace machinery, making cross product lemmas directly applicable without coercions.
mathContext: $\text{dot}(u,v) = \sum_{i<3} u_i v_i$, $\text{projPerp}(u,w)_i = u_i - (u \cdot w) w_i$, $\text{tripleProduct}(a,b,c) = a \cdot (b \times c) = \det[a,b,c]$.

title: Lagrange's Identity: |u×v|² = |u|²|v|² − (u·v)²
content: Lagrange's identity is the key algebraic relationship between the cross product norm and the dot product: |u×v|² = |u|²|v|² − (u·v)². The Lean proof expands everything using simp with [crossProduct, Fin.sum_univ_three] (which replaces finite sums by the three explicit terms) and then closes by ring. This identity is used twice: once in normSq_projPerp_unit (to show |projPerp u w|² ≥ 0 via the nonnegativity of |u×w|²) and again in sin_sq_dihedralAngle (to compute the Cauchy-Schwarz bound). It is the bridge between cross product geometry and inner product algebra.

title: normSq_projPerp_unit: |projPerp u w|² = sin²(arcLen u w)
content: For unit vectors u, w, the squared norm of the perpendicular projection of u onto the plane ⊥ w equals sin²(arcLen u w). The proof: (1) normSq_projPerp gives |projPerp u w|² = |u|² − (u·w)² = 1 − (u·w)²; (2) arcLen u w = arccos(u·w) and sin(arccos(x)) = √(1−x²) (Real.sin_arccos, which requires no bounds — valid for all real x); (3) √(1−x²)² = 1−x² for 0 ≤ 1−x². The nonnegativity 0 ≤ 1 − (u·w)² follows from Lagrange's identity: |u×w|² = 1·1 − (u·w)² ≥ 0. Notably, Real.sin_arccos in Lean 4 Mathlib requires no domain hypothesis — it holds for all x ∈ ℝ by convention (arccos is extended outside [-1,1]).

title: projPerp_cross_eq: The Key Identity for the Law of Sines
content:
This is the mathematical heart of the proof: projPerp(B,A) × projPerp(C,A) = det[A,B,C] · A. Geometrically: both projections lie in the plane perpendicular to unit vector A, so their cross product must be parallel to A (as the normal to that plane). The coefficient is the scalar triple product det[A,B,C].

Algebraically, component i of LHS − RHS equals (1 − |A|²)·(B×C)ᵢ, which vanishes when |A| = 1. The Lean proof verifies this component by component using funext + fin_cases i, expanding everything with simp [crossProduct, Fin.sum_univ_three, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul], and then closing each case with linear_combination −(Bⱼ·Cₖ − Bₖ·Cⱼ) · h where h : A₀²+A₁²+A₂² = 1.

The use of tripleProduct A B C • A (scalar multiplication) rather than fun i => tripleProduct A B C * A i is necessary for correct Lean 4 parsing — the notation avoids operator precedence conflicts with the equality sign.
mathContext: $\text{projPerp}(B,A) \times \text{projPerp}(C,A) = \det[A,B,C] \cdot A$. Proof: $(\text{LHS})_i - \det[A,B,C] \cdot A_i = (1 - |A|^2)(B \times C)_i = 0$ for unit $A$.

title: sin_sq_dihedralAngle: Connecting the Dihedral Angle to the Triple Product
content:
The dihedral angle α at vertex A is defined as the angle between the projections projPerp(B,A) and projPerp(C,A): α = arccos(pB·pC / (|pB|·|pC|)). The theorem proves sin²(α) = det[A,B,C]² / (|projPerp B A|² · |projPerp C A|²).

Proof outline: (1) using Real.sin_arccos (no bounds needed), sin²(arccos(x)) = 1−x² for all x; (2) with x = pB·pC/(|pB||pC|), we need 1 − (pB·pC)²/(|pB||pC|)² = det²/(|pB|²·|pC|²); (3) this rearranges to |pB|²·|pC|² − (pB·pC)² = det², which follows from: Lagrange's identity gives |pB×pC|² = |pB|²|pC|² − (pB·pC)², and normSq_projPerp_cross gives |pB×pC|² = det².

The Cauchy-Schwarz check (pB·pC)² ≤ (|pB||pC|)² ensures the argument of arccos lies in [-1,1], making the degenerate case branch (returning 0) irrelevant under the nonzero hypotheses.

title: spherical_law_of_sines_all_sq: All Three Ratios Equal
content:
spherical_law_of_sines_sq proves sin²(a)/sin²(α) = sin²(b)/sin²(β) by expressing both as det²/(sin²(a)·sin²(b)·sin²(c)) · common_factor and canceling via field_simp. The key observations: sin²(arcLen B C) = |projPerp C B|² (from sin_sq_arcLen), sin²(dih A B C) = det²/(|projPerp B A|²·|projPerp C A|²) (from sin_sq_dihedralAngle), and |projPerp B A|² = |projPerp A B|² (since both equal sin²(arcLen A B)).

spherical_law_of_sines_all_sq obtains the third equality by applying the two-ratio theorem to the relabeled triangle (B,C,A). The key insight: tripleProduct B C A = tripleProduct A B C (cyclic symmetry, tripleProduct_cyclic), so det² is unchanged. The dihedral angle rewrites use explicit instantiation (dihedralAngle_B_comm A B C).symm to avoid pattern-matching interference between the two rewrite steps.

The statement is in squared form (sin²/sin²) to avoid complications with signs and square roots, which is mathematically equivalent to the ratio form for the non-degenerate case.
mathContext: $\frac{\sin^2 a}{\sin^2 \alpha} = \frac{\sin^2 a \cdot \sin^2 b \cdot \sin^2 c}{\det^2} = \frac{\sin^2 b}{\sin^2 \beta} = \frac{\sin^2 c}{\sin^2 \gamma}$, using $\det[A,B,C] = \det[B,C,A] = \det[C,A,B]$.
